next_direction: REORIENT TO LIBRARIAN. Ruled direction from Akien: (1) keep cleaning up messes as found; (2) build out the librarian for deep research — go find out what's available, read understanding into graph trees; (3) both parts of the reader working and expanding; (4) work with hex to provide nodes to graph trees — the trees answer questions, hex furnishes the resolution; (5) no cognitive enhancements until the above works well enough to share and demonstrates the ideas. THE LIBRARIAN IS AN AGENT with his own agentic loop, graph trees as memory, personality that develops over time. Hex is his inference provider, not his intelligence — the intelligence lives in the trees and grows. The loop: receive question → walk trees → use tools (search, read, fetch) for raw material → feed through hex to get nodes → add to trees → answer from enriched trees. Build the loop ourselves (inference pipeline to hex exists, graph trees exist, the missing piece is conversation manager + tool dispatch + node-creation seam). SHARPEST DEMO: ask him something he doesn't know, watch him search/read/build nodes through hex, answer poorly. Ask again later — he answers well from his trees. He LEARNED. That's what nobody else is showing with a local 30B.
